rows.name: full match
rows.note: Deliberately different CASE on the two digests: hex comparison is case-insensitive, and a host doing an ordinal compare invalidates every cached bundle whose vault sha is upper-case.

rows.name: size mismatch wins over sha
rows.note: size is the cheapest discriminator and is checked first

rows.name: missing wins over everything
rows.note: every downstream discriminator has grounds to fire; Missing still wins. Pins the head of the precedence chain instead of implying it.

rows.name: sha mismatch wins over manifest too old
rows.note: pins sha256Mismatch > manifestTooOld — with the size-over-sha and missing-over-everything rows, the whole `precedence` list is now exercised, not implied.

rows.name: manifest too old
rows.note: v17 was the supported floor until the v18 hygiene bump; a bundle cached under it is stale now. The 'too old' row must always sit exactly one below minSupportedManifestVersion, so a bump that forgets this file is caught by the host asserting its own floor constant against minSupportedManifestVersion.

rows.name: legacy, everything unknown
rows.note: NULL SHA256 MEANS UNKNOWN, NOT ABSENT: skip the check, stay valid, and report integrityChecked=false. Failing here would make every legacy bundle un-openable.

rows.name: advertised sha but nothing computed (over the hash cap)
rows.note: valid but unverified — the host MUST say so rather than claim verification

rows.name: size mismatch with no sha advertised
rows.note: Size alone is enough to invalidate. The sha leg being unknown must not rescue a file that is demonstrably the wrong length.

rows.name: size mismatch with a sha advertised but uncomputed
rows.note: distinct from the over-cap row: there the size MATCHED and the entry stayed valid-but-unverified. Here the advertised-but-uncomputed sha must not soften a size mismatch into 'unverified'.
